title: Atomic‐Scale Insights Into the Thermal Stability of High‐Entropy Nanoalloys

recollection.starting_material: GUESS: equimolar CoCrFeMnNi high‐entropy alloy nanoparticles (3–5 nm in diameter)
recollection.intervention: GUESS: in situ annealing from room temperature up to 800 °C inside an aberration‐corrected scanning TEM, complemented by molecular‐dynamics/DFT simulations
recollection.structure: GUESS: retained single‐phase face‐centered cubic (fcc) lattice with minor surface or grain‐boundary segregation of Cr and Mn
recollection.mechanism: GUESS: sluggish diffusion arising from severe local lattice distortions and high mixing entropy suppresses coarsening and phase separation
recollection.results: GUESS: determined an effective activation energy for atomic diffusion of ≈1.8 eV, a coarsening exponent of ≈0.25, and observed <15% nanoparticle size increase after 100 h at 700 °C

score.note: The recollection partially identifies in situ heating with aberration-corrected STEM and simulations, but gives an incorrect temperature range and adds DFT. It misidentifies the alloy, incorrectly claims FCC retention and Cr/Mn segregation, and proposes sluggish diffusion and entropy stabilization—the opposite of the observed active diffusion, Au/Cu surface segregation, melting/evaporation, and kinetic control. All numerical results are incorrect; the actual study reported heating to 973 K and a 22% size reduction.
